lesson.title: Your data, your bundle
lesson.subtitle: What an agent costs in data, money and privacy

video.title: Your data, your bundle
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education, Bangladesh (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: Bundle gone; Sent far away; Another way?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A student of mine used up her whole data bundle in a week. Not on videos: on chatting with an AI agent! Every question went to a big computer far away. Is there another way?

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: what an agent costs in data, money and privacy, and how to choose.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Big agents run in the cloud: huge models on computers far away. Your question travels there and back over the network. Darsi Tiny is different: it runs on your phone, so nothing leaves it.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Take one weather request. Darsi Tiny reads about sixty tokens and answers in about a second, with no data. A cloud model reads about two and a half thousand, since the tools are described every time. That’s about eighteen kilobytes, and five seconds on 2G.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: At twenty requests a day, a month of cloud requests is about eleven megabytes. Darsi Tiny’s one download is two point eight megabytes. After about a hundred and fifty requests, the cloud has used more.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: You can work this out in Python. Multiply the kilobytes for one request by the requests a day and the days. Then divide by a thousand for megabytes: ten point eight.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! You’re on a bus with no signal, and you want to ask an agent something. Which one can still answer?

scenes.visual: A list: Works with no signal; Knows only ten tools; Big models know far more; Choose for the job.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The small model on your phone: it doesn’t need a signal. But remember what it can’t do. Darsi Tiny knows ten school tools and almost nothing else. A big cloud model knows far more, and that’s the trade.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Cost isn’t only money. Whatever you type into a cloud agent leaves your phone and is stored on someone else’s computers. It may be kept, read by staff, or used to train the next model.

scenes.visual: A list: Passwords and codes; Address, phone, ID number; Other people’s private things.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So never type these into a cloud agent. Your passwords and codes. Your address, phone number or ID number. And other people’s private things: a friend’s photo, their marks, their secrets.

scenes.visual: A list: Measure a request on your phone; Switch to 2G: compare the cloud; Your price, a whole month.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: what an agent costs
scenes.narration: In the app, run the weather request and note the tokens and the time. Switch to 2G and compare the cloud. Then set your data price and requests a day, and see a month.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. You want help with your diary, which is full of private thoughts. Where is it safest to ask?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Cloud: data, money, a signal; Phone: cheap, private, knows little; Never: passwords, others’ secrets.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Cloud: data, money, a signal · Phone: cheap, private, knows little · Never: passwords, others’ secrets
scenes.narration: On your phone, or not at all. Remember: cloud agents cost data, money and a signal, and your words leave the phone. Phone models are cheap and private, but know little. Never type passwords or others’ secrets.

scenes.visual: A list: Check last month’s data; Guess one AI app’s share; One thing you’ll never type.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: check how much data your phone used last month, and on which apps. Guess how much went on one AI app. Then decide one thing you will never type into it.

checkpoints.prompt: You’re on a bus with no signal and want to ask an agent something. Which one can still answer?

options.text: A big model in the cloud
A small model on your phone

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a model on your phone needs no signal and no data. It knows much less than a big cloud model, though.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a cloud model needs the network for every question. The small model runs on the phone itself.

checkpoints.prompt: You want help with your diary, which is full of private thoughts. Where is it safest to ask?

options.text: A cloud chatbot: it knows more
A model on your phone, or nobody
A cloud chatbot, in a new chat

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — whatever you type into a cloud chatbot leaves your phone, even in a new chat. Private thoughts stay on your phone, or with you.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a new chat still sends your words to someone else’s computers. Keep private thoughts on your phone, or to yourself.
